info.title: Valendata REST API
info.description: Create, run, schedule, and improve skills and workflows over JSON and HTTPS. Every route is under `/v1`; changes inside v1 are additive only (new routes, new optional parameters, new response fields). A route that will go away is marked `deprecated` here and answers with `Deprecation`, `Sunset` and a `Link` to its replacement for at least six months before it is removed. Errors, limits, pagination and idempotency: https://docs.valendata.com/api-reference/errors.

get.description: Your credit balance (exact, as a decimal string), plan and monthly allowance, the low-credit flag, auto-recharge, and your workspaces. Needs `account:read`.

Apps you can connect (Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack, Notion, HubSpot and hundreds more), each with `connected` (you have) and `connectable` (its sign-in works on Valendata today). Search with `q`; page with `limit` (1–50, default 25) and `cursor`. Needs `apps:read`.

apps.name: Google Calendar
apps.description: Google Calendar is a time management and scheduling service.

apps.name: Calendly
apps.description: Calendly is an appointment scheduling tool.

get.description: The apps you connected, each with `status`: `active` (it works) or `expired` (its sign-in lapsed; connect it again with the `connect_url` from `GET /v1/apps/{app}`). Needs `apps:read`.

One app, by id (`gmail`) or name (`Google Calendar`): whether you connected it, whether it can be connected, and `connect_url`, the page that connects it. Open it signed in to Valendata, then sign in to the app. The link does not expire, so you can send it to yourself. Needs `apps:read`.

200.description: The app and the link that connects it.

delete.description: Remove your connection to the app. Its sign-in is deleted, and its tools stop working (for you, your workflows and your assistants) until you connect it again. `disconnected` is `false` when it was not connected. Needs `apps:write`.

get.description: The app's tools, most used first, each with its `inputs` and `kind`: `read` (only reads) or `write` (sends, creates, changes, or deletes something). Page with `limit` and `cursor`. With `q`, a task in plain words, you get only the few tools that do it, best first, plus a `plan` and `pitfalls`, with no paging. Needs `apps:read`.

parameters.name: q

schema.description: A task in plain words: only the tools that do it, best first, with a plan (no paging).
schema.title: Q

parameters.description: A task in plain words: only the tools that do it, best first, with a plan (no paging).

tools.name: Fetch emails
tools.description: Fetches emails from the mailbox, filtered by a Gmail search query.

inputs.name: query
inputs.description: Gmail search query, e.g. is:unread from:boss@example.com.

pitfalls: Without a query, the newest emails of every sender come back.

post.description: Run one tool on your connected account with `inputs`, and get what the app answered in `data`. A `read` tool needs `apps:read`; a `write` tool needs `apps:write` and acts in your real account (an email is sent, an event is created), so send an `Idempotency-Key` to make a retry safe. `409` with code `app_not_connected` when you have not connected the app: `detail.connect_url` connects it. `502` when the app refused the call (`detail` says why).

preview.body: Here is the plan for Q4…

post.description: Wait for something to arrive, or check back later. `where.kind` says where it will land: `inbox` (your Valendata address), `email_app` (a connected mail app, by its `address`), `app_tool` (a read tool of a connected app, run with `arguments` on each check), `webpage` (a page that will change, by `url`), `run` (a workflow run reaching its end, by `run_id`), or `time` (nothing to look in: a check-back when `within` is up). `match` says what counts as arrived: its `kind` (`code`, `link`, `file`, `message`, `any`) and the sender's domain, address, recipient, or words it must contain. Only things that arrive after now count. `within` (at most 72 hours) is how long to wait, `check_every` how often to look. Answers `201` with the follow-up as `waiting`; poll `GET /v1/followups/{followup_id}` for its outcome (nothing calls you back). Up to 25 waiting at once. Needs `followups:write`, plus `apps:read` for `email_app` and `app_tool` (each check reads the app and costs the app-call price). `409` with code `app_not_connected` when the app is not connected: `detail.connect_url` connects it.

201.description: The follow-up, waiting. Poll `GET /v1/followups/{followup_id}` for its outcome.

get.description: Your follow-ups, newest first: the waiting ones, or every one with `active=false`. `kind` keeps one kind of place (`inbox`, `email_app`, `app_tool`, `webpage`, `run`, `time`); `agent` keeps one kind of waiter (`api` for follow-ups made here, `igris`, `session` or `brain` for ones your in-app agents made). Page with `limit` (1–100) and `cursor`. Needs `followups:read`.

parameters.name: active

schema.description: Only follow-ups still waiting (default). `false`: every one.
schema.title: Active

parameters.description: Only follow-ups still waiting (default). `false`: every one.

parameters.name: kind

schema.description: Only follow-ups looking in this kind of place.
schema.title: Kind

parameters.description: Only follow-ups looking in this kind of place.

parameters.name: agent

schema.description: Only follow-ups made by this kind of agent.
schema.title: Agent

parameters.description: Only follow-ups made by this kind of agent.

get.description: One follow-up: `status` (`waiting`, `done`, `cancelled`, `failed`), and once it ended, `outcome` (`found`, `time_up`, `expired`) with `found` holding only the thing that arrived — the code, link, file or a short excerpt — never the rest of the mailbox. `note` is one plain line on how it ended. Only your own; anyone else gets 404. Needs `followups:read`.

200.description: The follow-up: once it ended, its outcome and what was found.

post.description: Call a waiting follow-up off: no more checks, and it ends as `cancelled`. One that already ended is left as it is (`cancelled: false`). Needs `followups:write`.

200.description: Cancelled, or left as it was because it had already ended.

post.description: Start your skills and workflows to run in the background, each as a job with its own status. One item starts one job; two or more start a batch (`batch`) that ends when they all have. The answer comes at once (202) with the jobs; poll each with `GET /v1/jobs/{job_id}` (or the batch). An item that cannot start is listed in `refused` and the others still start; when none can, 422. Research helpers start from a chat, not the API. Needs `jobs:write`, plus `skills:invoke` / `workflows:invoke` for what you start.

get.description: Your background jobs, newest first: skill runs, workflow runs and research that your in-app agents (the assistant, a chat session) or you over the API started to run on their own. `open=true` keeps the ones still `queued` or `running`; `origin_kind` (`session`, `igris`, `brain`, `api`) and `origin_id` keep the ones one agent or chat started. Page with `limit` (1–100) and `cursor`. Needs `jobs:read`.

parameters.name: open

schema.description: Only jobs still queued or running. Default: every one.
schema.title: Open

parameters.description: Only jobs still queued or running. Default: every one.

parameters.name: origin_kind

schema.description: Only jobs started by this kind of caller.
schema.title: Origin Kind

parameters.description: Only jobs started by this kind of caller.

parameters.name: origin_id

schema.description: Only jobs started by this session or workflow.
schema.title: Origin Id

parameters.description: Only jobs started by this session or workflow.

200.description: A page of your background jobs.

get.description: One job: `status` (`queued`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`), and once it ended, `summary` (one plain line), `result` (`count` and a `preview` of the first rows) and `error`. `run_ref` is the run it drives: `GET /v1/runs/{run_id}` has every row. Only your own; anyone else gets 404. Needs `jobs:read`.

200.description: The job: once it ended, its summary and result.

post.description: Stop an open job and the run it drives; it ends as `cancelled` (rows the run already produced are kept). The answer is the job as it is now: `cancel_requested: true` while it stops. One that already ended is left as it is. Needs `jobs:write`.

200.description: The job as it is now: stopping, or left as it was because it had already ended.

post.description: Save a website login for your skills to sign in with. Stored encrypted in your Vault, never shared with your workspace, never returned. Needs a session or an API key with `logins:write`.

get.description: Your saved logins, masked — never a password, seed or code. A login an agent registered itself (auto sign-up) says so, and whether its sign-up was confirmed. Needs `logins:use` or `logins:write`.

One saved login, masked: the site, a hint of the username, its label and notes, whether it has an authenticator seed, and — for one an agent registered itself — whether its sign-up was confirmed. Needs `logins:use` or `logins:write`.

patch.description: Send a new password, username or authenticator seed. Nothing secret comes back.

delete.description: Deletes the login. Skills that signed in with it stop doing so.

get.summary: Find a skill for a task
get.description: Skills that do the task in `q`, best first, from the public marketplace and (with `skills:read`) your own and your workspaces' (`yours: true`). Each result has its inputs, `price` (the typical cost of its recent runs in credits and dollars, or its base price before any run), `health` (success rate over its last 20 runs) and the route to run it. Matching reads the meaning of `q`, not only its words. When nothing does the task, the closest skills come back with `match: "near"` and a `hint`. No key needed for the public marketplace.

schema.description: The task, in your words: 'find LinkedIn jobs in Toronto'

get.description: Your notes: pinned first, then the most recently changed. With `q`, only the notes matching any of its words (in the title, body, tags or topic), best match first, at most the best 200. `topic`, `tag` and `pinned` keep only the notes that have them. Each note comes in full. Page with `limit` (1–100) and `cursor`. Needs `notes:read`. `503` until notes are switched on for your account.

schema.description: Words to search for in the title, body, tags and topic. Matches come best first.

post.description: Write a new note on your Notes page: a `title`, a Markdown `body` (tables and checklists work), and optionally a `topic`, `tags` and `pinned`. Give a title or a body; without a title, the body's first line becomes it. Tags are kept lowercase, each once. The note is marked `source: api`. Answers `201` with the note. Needs `notes:write`.

get.description: One note in full: its title, Markdown body, topic, tags, whether it is pinned, who wrote it first (`source`), when, and `link`, its page in the app. Only your own; anyone else gets 404. Needs `notes:read`.

example.title: Dinner split 27 Sep

| --- | --- | --- |
| Ada | 12,000 | paid |

patch.description: Change a note; only what you send changes. The body changes one way per request: `body` replaces all of it, `append` adds text at the end (on the next line when it continues a list or a table), or `find` with `replace_with` changes one exact place, such as a table row. `find` must appear exactly once, or nothing changes and you get 422. Also sets `title`, `topic` (empty clears it), `tags` (replaces them; an empty list clears them) and `pinned`. Answers with the note as it is now. Only your own; anyone else gets 404. Needs `notes:write`.

200.description: The note as it is now.

delete.description: Delete a note for good; it cannot be brought back. Answers with its id and title and `deleted: true`. Only your own; anyone else gets 404. Needs `notes:write`.

200.description: The note is gone for good.

get.description: Any run, skill or workflow: its status, and the result once it has finished. Skill runs hold their rows in `rows`; workflow runs hold `outputs` and have `kind: "workflow"`. Needs `runs:read` for a skill run, `workflows:read` for a workflow run.

post.description: Stop a queued or running run you started: a skill run, or a workflow run and what it is running inside. Rows already produced are kept. A finished run is left as it is (`cancelled: false`). Needs `skills:invoke` for a skill run, `workflows:invoke` for a workflow run.

When a site texts a sign-in code, the run waits up to 3 minutes for it. Send it here; the run types it into the page and carries on. A skill creation (`sc_…`) signing in or up waits the same way: send its creation id. Only the account that started it. Needs `logins:use` on an API key.

get.description: Every schedule you may see, skills' and workflows'. `kind` narrows it to `skill` or `workflow`. A kind your key has no read scope for is left out.

schema.title: Response Get Schedule Api V1 Schedules  Schedule Id  Get

get.description: One schedule. Skill schedule ids start with `sklsch_`, workflow schedule ids with `wfsch_`.

patch.description: Change `cron` or `every`, `timezone`, `inputs`, `enabled`, or (skill schedules only) `max_results`. Only what you send changes. Needs `skills:write` or `workflows:write`; switching a workflow schedule on also needs `workflows:invoke`.

schema.title: Response Update Schedule Api V1 Schedules  Schedule Id  Patch

delete.description: Turn the schedule off and forget its settings. The skill or workflow stays.

parameters.name: status

schema.description: Comma-separated statuses, e.g. needs_fix,failed; active = queued, recording and validating.
schema.title: Status

parameters.description: Comma-separated statuses, e.g. needs_fix,failed; active = queued, recording and validating.

200.description: A page of your skill creations.

get.description: Your skill creations, newest first, each as `GET /v1/skill-creations/{creation_id}` answers it (without `sample_rows`). Filter with `status` — a comma list, or `active` for every creation still in progress (`queued`, `recording`, `validating`) — and page with `limit` (1–100, default 20) and `cursor`. Only your own creations are listed.

Where a creation is: `queued`, `recording`, `validating`, `ready` (run `run_url`), `needs_fix` (the recording was saved as a draft skill with `sample_rows`, but its test replay did not pass — fix it with `POST /v1/skills/{slug}/improve`, do not create it again) or `failed` (nothing was saved; `error` says why). `progress` is the latest step in plain words and `credits_charged` what the creation has cost so far. `next_step` says what to do. Only the account that started it can read it.

Where an improvement is: `queued`, `working`, `validating`, `done` (`result` and `improved` say whether the new version is live; `changes` shows each field before → after; `details` shows new, merged and unclear fields) or `failed` (`error`). The account that started it and anyone who can edit the Skill (its owner or a workspace editor) can poll it; anyone else gets 404.

Your skills and those shared into your workspaces, newest first: each with its inputs, health over the last 20 runs, last run, and the routes to run it. Search with `q`, filter by `status`, and page with `limit` (1–100, default 50) and `cursor`. Needs `skills:read`.

parameters.name: q

schema.description: Text in the name, slug or description
schema.title: Q

parameters.description: Text in the name, slug or description

post.description: Record `task` in a cloud browser from `start_url` and publish it as a Skill. Answers at once with a creation id; poll `GET /v1/skill-creations/{creation_id}`. Up to 2 recordings in progress per account; needs at least 10 credits. Behind a sign-in, pass `login_id` (needs `logins:use`); without one the creation fails with `needs_user` (kind `no_login`) — unless auto sign-up is on, then it registers an account for the site with your Valendata email and binds it.

202.description: Creation started (or the existing one, for a repeated Idempotency-Key).

post.description: Older form of `POST /v1/skills/{slug}/run` that takes `skill_id` and `parameters` in the body. It still works. New code should use the slug route.

parameters.name: max_results

schema.description: Max rows to return; 0 means the entire list. Omit to use the skill's saved default.
schema.title: Max Results

parameters.description: Max rows to return; 0 means the entire list. Omit to use the skill's saved default.

get.description: The skill and its contract: `input_schema`, `output_json_schema`, `reliability`, versions, and fast path. A public skill needs no key. A private skill returns 404 to anyone who may not run it.

patch.description: Change a skill's name, description, inputs, output fields, run settings, saved login, or sharing. Only what you send changes. Answers with the skill as `GET /v1/skills/{slug}` returns it, plus `changes`, `warnings`, and `login`. Owner or workspace editor; `login_id` and `visibility` are owner only. Needs `skills:write` (and `logins:write` for `login_id`).

delete.description: Delete a skill you own. Its runs are kept (your billing history) and its schedule stops. If a workflow uses the skill, you get `409` listing those workflows, unless you pass `force=true`. Needs `skills:write`.

parameters.name: force

schema.description: Delete even though workflows use it (their step then fails)
schema.title: Force

parameters.description: Delete even though workflows use it (their step then fails)

post.description: Copy a public marketplace skill (or one shared into your workspace) into your own skills, so you can run it. Free. The copy is private and keeps its lineage; run it at `POST /v1/skills/{new slug}/run`. Answers with the copy as `GET /v1/skills/{slug}` shows it, plus `cloned_from`. Needs `skills:invoke` or `skills:write`.

get.description: Success rate and repairs over the last 20 runs, when it last worked, the last failure kind, the live recipe version, and each route's health. Public for public Skills; private Skills return 404 to anyone who may not run them.

post.description: Change a Skill in one of three modes. `fix` (default): relearn it from a plain-English hint about where the data is. `add_fields`: capture new fields you describe in plain English; the request is first compared with the Skill's fields, so a re-worded duplicate is merged into the existing field and an unclear one comes back as a question. `relearn_details`: rebuild how the Skill opens each result (its per-row detail steps), for when the site changed or detail fields come back empty. Every mode runs on a cloud browser, saves a new recipe version and checks it with a short run (up to 5 rows). The new version stays live only if it is better; otherwise it is kept as a candidate and the previous recipe stays live. Owner or workspace editor only; drafts allowed. One improvement at a time per account and per Skill, up to 6 an hour, at least 10 credits to start. Charged to the caller.

202.description: Improvement started (or the existing one, for a repeated Idempotency-Key).

get.description: The Skill's full change history, newest first: every fix, added field and re-learn by anyone allowed to edit it (the owner or a workspace editor), from any channel (`source`), plus past Refine and Re-learn entries imported from before (`imported: true`, `result: applied`).

200.description: The Skill's change history, newest first.

get.description: Whether the marketplace skill this copy came from has a newer version. A cloned skill, or one that came with a cloned workflow, is yours: the author's later changes never reach it on their own. `reason` says why none is offered: `not_a_copy`, `source_gone`, or `up_to_date`. Owner or workspace only. Needs `skills:read`.

post.description: Take the newer marketplace version into your copy, merged onto your own changes and saved as a new version you can restore away from. Where you and the author changed the same step differently, nothing is applied: the update is saved as an unapplied version (`candidate_version`) for you to compare. Owner or workspace editor only. Needs `skills:write`.

put.description: `{"version": n}` pins the Skill to version `n`; `{"version": null}` unpins it. While pinned, automatic repairs are saved as candidate versions and do not change what runs. Owner or workspace editor only.

post.description: Run a published Skill and wait for the rows. Put the Skill's inputs at the top level of the JSON body (or in the query string). The body keys `browser_type`, `proxy_config`, `profile_id`, `scrape_mode`, `max_pages`, and `version` are run settings, not inputs. Inputs are checked against `input_schema` before anything runs. If too many of your runs are in progress, this returns 429 with `Retry-After` instead of waiting.

parameters.name: max_results

schema.description: Max rows to return; 0 means the entire list. Omit to use the skill's saved default.
schema.title: Max Results

parameters.description: Max rows to return; 0 means the entire list. Omit to use the skill's saved default.

parameters.name: max_pages
parameters.description: Page limit for paginated skills; 0 means all pages.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Recipe version to replay for this call.

schema.description: The skill's inputs at the top level, plus optional run settings: max_pages, version, browser_type, proxy_config, profile_id, scrape_mode.

post.description: Validate the inputs, start the run, and answer at once with a `run_id`. If your account is at its limit of runs in progress, the run queues. Poll `GET /v1/runs/{run_id}` or pass `webhook_url`.

202.description: Run queued (or the existing one, for a repeated Idempotency-Key).

get.description: A skill's runs, newest first. Filter by `status` (comma-separated) and `since`; page with `limit` (1–100, default 50) and `cursor`. The owner and workspace see every run; someone running a public skill sees their own. Needs `runs:read`.

parameters.name: since

schema.description: Only runs started at or after this time
schema.title: Since

parameters.description: Only runs started at or after this time

get.description: The skill's schedule, as a list of zero or one: a skill has one schedule. Needs `skills:read`.

post.description: Run a skill on a schedule. Give exactly one of `cron` or `every`, a `timezone`, the `inputs` each run uses (checked now), and `max_results` (default 100). `409` if the skill already has a schedule: change it with `PATCH /v1/schedules/{schedule_id}`. Each run spends the owner's credits. Needs `skills:write`.

get.description: Every recipe version, newest first, with which one is live and which is pinned. Needs the right to run the Skill.

schema.title: Response Diff Versions V1 Skills  Slug  Versions  A  Diff  B  Get

get.description: What changed from version `a` to version `b`.

post.description: Make version `n` the live recipe. The restore is saved as a new version. Owner or workspace editor only.

get.description: Credits spent per UTC day and per source between `from` and `to` (default the last 30 days, at most 366). Refunds are taken off; goodwill refunds for old over-charges are reported separately in `goodwill_refunds`. Needs `account:read`.

The secret your webhook deliveries are signed with. Each delivery carries `X-Valendata-Timestamp` and `X-Valendata-Signature: v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<timestamp>.<raw body>")>`. Needs the `webhooks:read` scope when called with an API key. For 24 hours after a rotation the signature header carries two comma-separated values, new first.

post.description: Replace the signing secret with a new random one and return it. The previous secret keeps signing deliveries (as a second comma-separated `v1=` value) until `previous_valid_until`, 24 hours from now. Needs the `webhooks:write` scope when called with an API key.

get.description: Older form of `GET /v1/runs/{run_id}` for workflow runs. It still works. New code should use `/v1/runs/{run_id}`.

schema.title: Response Get Workflow Run V1 Workflow Runs  Run Id  Get

get.description: Workflows you own and those shared with you through a workspace, newest first. Search with `q`; page with `limit` (1–100, default 25) and `cursor`. Needs `workflows:read`.

post.description: Create a workflow from its inputs, steps, and connections. Every step, connection, skill or workflow reference, and `{{inputs.x}}` is checked first; a `422` lists every problem and nothing is saved. A key limited to some workflows cannot create one. Needs `workflows:write`.

get.description: A workflow and its contract: inputs, output shape, track record, routes, and its MCP tool name. `include_graph=true` adds its steps and connections.

parameters.name: include_graph

schema.description: Also return steps, connections and version.
schema.title: Include Graph

parameters.description: Also return steps, connections and version.

patch.description: Change a workflow's name, description, inputs, steps, or connections. Only what you send changes; `steps` replaces the whole list. The state before is kept as a version you can restore in the app. Owner or workspace owner, admin, or member. Needs `workflows:write`.

delete.description: Delete a workflow you own and take its schedule off. Its runs are kept and stay readable with GET /v1/runs/{run_id}. This cannot be undone. Needs `workflows:write`.

post.description: Copy a public marketplace workflow (or one shared into your workspace) into your own workflows, so you can run it. Free. The copy is a private draft and keeps its lineage. The skills and sub-workflows it runs that are not yours come along as copies of your own, so the author's later changes never reach it; `copied` lists them, and the steps that need your own login or credential. Answers with the copy as `GET /v1/workflows/{slug}` shows it, plus `cloned_from` and `copied`. Needs `workflows:invoke` or `workflows:write`.

Checks the inputs against the workflow's declared inputs (a bad call is a 422 and costs nothing), runs it, and waits up to `wait` seconds (default 60, max 120). Finished in time → 200 with `outputs`. Still running → 202 with the run so far; poll its `status_url`. If your account is at its limit of runs in progress, the answer is 429 with `Retry-After` (use `/runs` to queue instead).

Checks the inputs, starts the run and answers at once with a `run_id`. If your account is at its limit of runs in progress, the run waits as `pending`. Poll `GET /v1/workflow-runs/{run_id}` or pass `webhook_url` to receive the finished run as a signed POST.

SkillImprovementStatus.title: SkillImprovementStatus
SkillImprovementStatus.description:
Where an improvement is: queued → working → validating → done | failed.

``done`` with ``improved: true`` means the new recipe version is live; ``done`` with
``improved: false`` means the attempt was kept as a candidate version (not live) and
``outcome`` says why. ``failed`` means the engine could not run (``error``). ``result``
says the same in one word.
